name: Benign Paroxysmal Tonic Upgaze of Childhood with Ataxia
aliases: Benign Paroxysmal Tonic Upgaze Syndrome with Ataxia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Benign Paroxysmal Tonic Upgaze of Childhood

criteria.description: Paroxysmal episodes of sustained upward deviation of the eyes lasting seconds to minutes
Presence of cerebellar ataxia manifesting as gait instability or limb incoordination
Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions
No evidence of epileptic seizures or abnormal EEG findings
Spontaneous resolution or marked improvement by early childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of paroxysmal tonic upgaze episodes and cerebellar ataxia with exclusion of structural brain abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by normal neuroimaging and EEG; genetic testing may be considered to exclude other causes.

imaging: Normal brain MRI without structural abnormalities
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; genetic testing may exclude other ataxias

distinguishingFeatures: Sustained upward eye deviation lasting hours
Often drug-induced or secondary to metabolic disorders
Progressive ataxia rather than benign course
Associated developmental delay and cognitive impairment

references: Orphanet: Benign Paroxysmal Tonic Upgaze of Childhood with Ataxia (ORPHA:1179)
Bertini E, et al. Benign paroxysmal tonic upgaze of childhood: clinical features and outcome. Neurology. 2001.
Kheradmand A, Zee DS. Benign paroxysmal tonic upgaze of childhood: a review. J Child Neurol. 2010.
